hypothesis: If the claim holds, the genus-level faunal similarity of fossil assemblages falls as the time separation between their stages grows, so assemblages from consecutive stages share far more genera than assemblages from widely separated stages.
pass_criterion: Take PBDB marine invertebrate occurrences with accepted genus names, assigned to International Chronostratigraphic Chart stages (Cambrian Stage 2 to Pleistocene), with at least 100 genera per stage. Compute the Jaccard similarity of the genus sets for every stage pair. The claim is confirmed if the median Jaccard for consecutive stage pairs (lag 1) is at least 2 times the median for pairs separated by 5 or more stages (lag >=5). It must also hold that the Spearman correlation between similarity and lag across all pairs is <= -0.5, and that for at least 80% of interior stages the similarity to an adjacent stage exceeds the similarity to any stage 5 or more steps away.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if the lag-1 median Jaccard is less than 1.5 times the lag>=5 median, or the Spearman correlation between similarity and lag is above -0.3, or fewer than 60% of interior stages are more similar to an adjacent stage than to stages 5 or more steps away. Results between these bounds count as inconclusive and as not confirming the claim. The same test is repeated with a Sorensen index and with a sampling-standardised subset (subsampling to 100 occurrences per stage), and the verdict must agree across all three variants.
interpretation: Darwin's 'formation' is mapped to a geological stage, the nearest modern unit with a numeric age. Formations themselves are recorded only as free text in PBDB, and many lack a precise age. 'Closely related' fossils are mapped to the share of genera two assemblages have in common, measured by the Jaccard index, because genus names are the most consistently recorded taxonomic rank. Taxonomic relatedness in the sense of descent is not measured directly. 'Far more' is operationalised as a ratio of at least 2. 'Remote' means a separation of 5 or more stages. 'Broadly intermediate' is operationalised by the adjacent-stage criterion. This is a modern reinterpretation. It is vulnerable to sampling bias, because stages differ in rock volume and in sampling, and to taxonomic oversplitting. The standardised subsampling variant addresses part of this.

dataset.name: The Paleobiology Database (PBDB) Data Service, fossil occurrences
dataset.why_it_fits: The PBDB occurrences endpoint (data1.2/occs/list.csv or .json) returns fossil occurrences with the fields accepted_name, genus, early_interval, late_interval, max_ma, min_ma, formation, phylum and class. These fields allow genus lists to be built per stage and the Jaccard similarity to be computed as a function of stage lag. The service is open, needs no registration, and can be queried by taxon, interval and rank.
